summary: Source-anchored research for Concept knowledge architecture strategies. Run status: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.

facts.text: AIS evaluates whether a generated statement is attributable to identified parts of an underlying source corpus. (low confidence)
AIS permits support from multiple source parts combined through reasoning such as arithmetic. (low confidence)
TREC test collections contain a document corpus, information needs, and relevance judgments. (low confidence)
Bitemporal history separates when a fact applies in the modeled world from when the system recorded it. (medium confidence)
ALCE assigns statement-level citation recall only when the cited passages jointly entail the whole statement. (low confidence)
ALCE's automatic precision method can falsely penalize a citation that partially supports a statement when other citations also cover that information. (low confidence)
Claimify can decline extraction when context does not resolve competing interpretations with sufficient confidence. (low confidence)
The late-chunking paper finds no benefit when surrounding document text is irrelevant to the target information. (low confidence)
Long late chunking uses overlapping long-context windows when the document exceeds the embedding model's context capacity. (low confidence)
During screening, true recall remains unknown until all candidate documents have been assessed because the total relevant-document count is unknown. (low confidence)
The query embedding model must match the intended stored embedding space when switching indexes. (medium confidence)
BEIR selected nDCG because it accommodates binary and graded relevance while respecting rank. (low confidence)
NIST requires the document collection and relevance-judgment set to match when evaluating a run. (low confidence)
